children: The U.S.-Iran war has pushed Bahrain's finances to the brink once again, Barclays analysts write. Bahrain's gross foreign reserves fell to just $1.75 billion in October, covering less than one month of imports, the analysts say. "Financial buffers are dangerously thin and it seems increasingly imminent that Gulf support will be provided to relieve pressure," Barclays writes. "The upshot is that financial buffers are dangerously low and cannot last at current depletion rates for much longer." Until a deal is finalized, however, pain in Bahrain's financial markets is set to continue, the analysts add. (joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)
